A **skill** is a reusable operating guide for a kind of work. It tells an agent when the skill applies, which tools and scripts to use, what order to follow, and where approval is required.

A skill is not the same thing as a tool:

- tools perform typed operations;
- skills explain how to combine operations well;
- scripts contain executable implementation.

## Two files define the basic contract

```text
my-skill/
  SKILL.md
  skill.json
```

`SKILL.md` is the guidance entrypoint. `skill.json` is compact metadata used for discovery, installation, permission checks, and registry generation.

## Loading is not execution

Reading a skill gives the agent instructions. It does not automatically run the scripts or tools named inside it.

Some skills also have a runtime runner callable through the OS skill execution surface. A declared skill without a current runner returns `SKILL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; do not assume every guidance skill is independently executable.

## Permissions stay aligned

Skill metadata includes a permission tier and `requiresApproval`. Validation checks that these values match the canonical manifest. A skill cannot claim a safer permission level than the operation exposed by its runtime entry.

## Installed skills

Bundled skills selected during setup are copied into:

```text
~/.consuelo/skills/
```

The compact installed registry is:

```text
~/.consuelo/skills/skills.json
```

User-owned local skill folders are preserved when OS is provisioned again.
